evidence.quote:
Goal: callers can supply fixed occupied cells. Main choice: take a per-run set
snapshot and reject a forward target before changing pose. A blocked command
returns `False`; subsequent commands still run. Existing two-argument calls remain
compatible. For example, from `(0, 0, 1)` with `(1, 0)` occupied, `FRF` ends at
`(0, -1, 2)` with `[False, True, True]`.
Risks: accidentally appending `True` after blocking, checking full pose instead of coordinates, or retaining mutable caller occupancy.

Snapshot the supplied occupied coordinates into a local `frozenset` once per run, then reject occupied forward targets before changing pose. This avoids retaining mutable caller occupancy and keeps state local.

S1 adds optional occupancy to `navigator.run`, navigation tests, and README usage with a blocked-session example. It depends on D1.1 design review, plan review, and later implementation authorization; it is not implemented, tested, or reviewed.
A decisive exposed example: starting at `(0, 0, 1)` with `(1, 0)` occupied, `FRF` must finish at `(0, -1, 2)` with results `[False, True, True]`.
